info.title: Postal ID Verification API
info.description:
Validates Postal Identification cards against the enrollment database.

## How a verification works
Submit the details printed on a card. The service answers `VALID` when
a matching record exists, has not been deleted, has reached an issued
status, and the name and date of birth agree. Otherwise it answers
`INVALID`.

## What INVALID does not tell you
Every failing case returns the same body. The API will not say whether
a reference number exists or which field was wrong. This is deliberate:
a more helpful answer would let the endpoint be used to harvest
personal data belonging to other people.

## Images
A `VALID` response includes short-lived references to the cardholder's
photograph and signature. They expire within minutes and permit only a
few fetches. Fingerprints and supporting document scans are held in the
database but are not retrievable through this API under any scope.

## Rate limits
Requests are budgeted per client and per source address. Exceeding a
budget returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Checks the submitted details against the enrollment record identified by the
postal reference number, and answers VALID or INVALID.

VALID requires all of: a record with that reference number exists, it is not
deleted, it has reached an issued status, and the surname, first name, middle
name and date of birth all match.

Every unsuccessful case produces the same INVALID body. The endpoint will not
reveal whether the reference number exists or which field failed, because that
would make it usable for harvesting other people's details.

On VALID the response carries short-lived relative URLs for the cardholder's
photograph and signature. Fetching them needs the postalid.images scope.

200.description: Verification completed. Inspect `result` for the answer.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid access token.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded; see the Retry-After header.

get.description:
Streams the photograph or signature behind a reference returned by a VALID
verification.

References expire a few minutes after they are issued and allow only a small
number of fetches. Signatures and scans are held as TIFF, which browsers cannot
display, so they are converted to PNG on the way out; the JPEG photograph is
served as captured. Read the Content-Type header rather than assuming a format.

Only photographs and signatures can ever be referenced. Fingerprints and
supporting document scans are stored but not reachable through this API.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Opaque reference from a VALID verification response

200.description: Image bytes, as image/png or image/jpeg

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid access token

404.description: Reference is unknown, expired or exhausted

VerifyRequest.description: Details transcribed from a Postal ID card

postalRefNo.description: Postal reference number printed on the card

firstName.description: Given name as printed on the card

middleName.description: Middle name or initial; omit if the card shows none

lastName.description: Surname as printed on the card

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth in ISO-8601 form

VerifyResponse.description: Outcome of a Postal ID verification

result.description: VALID when the details match an issued Postal ID, INVALID otherwise

requestId.description: Correlation id, also written to the audit trail; quote it in support requests

images.description: Present only on VALID. Relative URLs for the cardholder's photo and signature, each usable for a short window.

imagesExpireIn.description: Present only on VALID. Seconds until the image URLs stop working.

oauth2-client-credentials.description:
OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Request a token from the token endpoint using
your client id and secret over HTTP Basic, then send it as a bearer token.
Tokens are short-lived; request a new one rather than caching indefinitely.
